extraction.name: Learning Multiple Layers of Features from Tiny Images
extraction.description: The paper describes training a multi-layer generative model of natural images and introduces the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets, which are labeled subsets of the 80 million tiny images dataset.
extraction.creator: Alex Krizhevsky
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The tiny images dataset was assembled by searching the web for images of every non-abstract English noun in the lexical database WordNet using several search engines, including Google, Flickr, and Altavista, keeping roughly the first 3000 results for each search term.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from the web found using search engines (Google, Flickr, and Altavista) based on non-abstract English nouns from WordNet.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Over the span of six months
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Removed perfect duplicates and images in which an excessively large portion of the pixels were white. Images were downscaled to 32x32.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data was preprocessed using a ZCA whitening transformation and by deleting the 1000 least significant principal components (directions of variance) from the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Students were paid to label a subset of the tiny images dataset. Each labeler was given a class and asked to examine all images found with that class (and its hyponyms) as the search term. Labelers were instructed to reject images that did not belong to their assigned class based on specific criteria (e.g., photo-realistic, only one prominent instance, class name is a likely answer to 'What is in this picture?').
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors personally verified every label submitted by the labelers and removed duplicate images from the dataset by comparing images with the L2 norm.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The search term used to find an image provides it with a rough label, although it is extremely unreliable due to the nature of online image search technology.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Unsupervised training of deep generative models, object recognition experiments, and classification.
